title: New `defaultindeterminate` attribute for <input type=checkbox>
body: Fixes #6578, which identified a gap where _indeterminateness_ could not be specified statically, blocking static HTML generators and server-side rendering processes from being able to use indeterminate checkboxes without resorting to invoking JavaScript. To fill this gap, I'm adding a `defaultindeterminate` content attribute that is reflected by a `defaultIndeterminate` IDL attribute (not the existing `indeterminate` IDL attribute). A _dirty indeterminateness_ concept is added, and parallels the existing concept of _dirty checkedness_, to allow interaction and usage of the `indeterminate` IDL attribute to separate the control from the "default" value. The name choice is in line with other groups' recent decisions, such as Open UI choosing `initiallyopen` over a live `open` content attribute (see https://github.com/openui/open-ui/issues/311#issuecomment-1050192589). It also helps address confusion around the (lack of) liveness between the content attribute and the actual value of the control. Additionally, introducing a new _dirty indeterminateness_ concept instead of overloading _dirty checkedness_ better matches existing user agent behavior, where the `indeterminate` IDL property doesn't establish _dirty checkedness_. User interaction would establish _dirty indeterminateness_, in addition to _dirty checkedness_.
